subject: Streaming chunk pacing & TTFT targets — post-demo recap
messages:
From: Mateo Álvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Perez <alyssa.perez@capitalgrid.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming chunk pacing & TTFT targets — post-demo recap

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap + technical clarifications so we can lock the pilot scope and the MW timeline. Looping Rafael/Stephanie for pricing & cadence and David for the integration checklist.

What we captured on the call (please confirm or correct):
- Primary SLO target: Time-to-first-token (TTFT) goal of 150 ms p95 for interactive flows (token streaming).
- Acceptable TTFT floor for MVP: 200 ms p95.
- Streaming transport: prefer WebSocket for sub-100ms steady-state latencies; SSE acceptable if proxies/firewalls force it.
- Chunk cadence (app-level): 200–350 ms per chunk is ideal for UX; 250 ms recommended starting point.
- Concurrency: expect ~25 concurrent live editors during peak; plan for safety headroom to 60 concurrent streams.
- Throughput: steady-state 60 rps, peak bursts up to 120 rps.
- Fallback behavior: want automatic fallback to shorter-context model variant to preserve TTFT under high load.

Attachments: Latency_Specs_v1.pdf (detailed perf numbers we referenced), SLA_Draft_CapitalGrid.docx (initial legal/ops).

Questions for CapitalGrid:
1) Do you have a strict requirement for SSE vs WebSocket (firewall/proxy constraints)?
2) Can you confirm expected payload sizes (average tokens generated per response) — we used 80 tokens avg in our sizing.
3) Any regulatory constraints that require Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) rather than Hosted?

Next steps (proposed):
- Alyssa confirms the 150 ms p95 TTFT target and transport preference (SSE vs WS).
- Redwood provides two run options: Hosted pilot with configuration tuned for ~200 ms (cost-efficient) and Dedicated reserved pool blueprint to meet 150 ms p95.
- Rafael to send pricing estimate and a one-month reserved trial snapshot; Stephanie to include SLA/credits language.
- David to send integration checklist and sample telemetry schema for our observability hooks.

If you confirm by end of week we can schedule the pilot kickoff for the week of 7/27.

—Mateo
Mateo Álvarez
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

From: Alyssa Perez <alyssa.perez@capitalgrid.com>
To: Mateo Álvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: CapitalGrid Platform Team <infra@capitalgrid.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 17:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming chunk pacing & TTFT targets — post-demo recap

Thanks Mateo — comprehensive recap, appreciated. A few clarifications from our side after internal alignment: 

- Target: We can commit to 200 ms p95 TTFT as the initial success metric for the pilot. 150 ms p95 is a stretch goal we want to explore if Dedicated is required.
- Transport: Corporate infra prefers SSE by default (outbound long-poll/SSE flows are easier through our proxies). WebSocket is allowed for select endpoints but requires additional firewall rules and an approval window. For the pilot, let's proceed with SSE and pilot a WS path for a small subset if needed.
- Chunk cadence: 300 ms cadence is fine for our UX team; they prefer slightly larger chunks over micro-chunks to reduce reflow.
- Concurrency & throughput: baseline concurrent editors 20–30, but plan for 50 concurrent as an operational headroom. Average tokens per response closer to 120 (we run some longer summarization flows). We expect avg steady-state 40 rps with bursts to 90 rps.
- Security/Compliance: we attached our Security Questionnaire; we're open to Hosted but may require Private for production if SOC2 evidence exposure becomes a concern.

Attachments: CapitalGrid_Security_Questionnaire.pdf

Next steps for us: confirm SSE for pilot, provide a sample payload size matrix this afternoon, and schedule a short dev-to-dev call to map telemetry. We can sign the SLA draft once pricing is aligned.

Thanks — Alyssa
Alyssa Perez
Head of Platform, CapitalGrid
alyssa.perez@capitalgrid.com | +1 (212) 555-0133

Thanks Alyssa — that's perfect and very helpful. Confirming items and listing immediate Redwood actions: 

- Pilot success metric: 200 ms p95 TTFT (pilot). Redwood will size hosted pilot to aim for 200 ms p95 with SSE transport and 300 ms chunk cadence per your UX ask.
- Stretch path: if you want to target 150 ms p95 we recommend a Dedicated reserved pool (we'll provide an A/B config: lower-latency GPU profile + greedy KV cache). Rafael — can you prepare the 30-day reserved trial pricing and the delta to meet 150 ms?
- Telemetry: David will send the observability payload schema this morning (traces, token-level latency, model variant id, request id). David — please include example curl/websocket snippets and the JSON schema for token chunk events.
- Security: received your questionnaire — our security team will start the review. If Hosted is acceptable for pilot we'll surface SOC2 artifacts; Private will require a slightly longer onboarding lead time.

Proposed timeline:
- 7/16: Redwood sends pricing snapshot + telemetry schema (Rafael/David).
- 7/19: Dev-to-dev call to wire up SSE endpoints and sample payloads (30–45m).
- 7/27: Pilot kickoff (2-week run) — run load up to 90 rps with controlled bursts to validate fallback behaviors.

We also included a short playbook link for TTFT troubleshooting: https://redwood.app/docs/ttft-playbook. Rafael, please attach the updated SLA language when you send pricing. Stephanie — please flag any corporate credit terms or exceptions.

If that schedule works I'll issue the HubSpot deal update and drop a DocuSign for the pilot SOW.

—Mateo
